seed_scope: Global FMath::RandInit before loading the map and before deferred clone spawning; not a guarantee of identical whole-engine stochastic traces.

npc_movement.scope: Actual NPC actors observed only inside the capture window from AfterFrame on the existing memory cadence. Initial/end positions refer to first/last movement samples. Distances are2D to exclude falling; sampled segment totals underestimate curved/full trajectories. Movement plus moving complete path is evidence for at least one actor, not a guarantee that every NPC walks or reaches every target.
npc_movement.nav_scope: Actual NPC agent properties select navigation data using the engine. Projection uses100/100/500 extent. Native DoesSupportAgent is recorded, not imposed as a stricter selection rule. Valid data requires valid bounds and, for Recast, native HasValidNavmesh. Projection and moving paths are separate evidence of traversable local navigation.
npc_movement.clone_position_scope: Original actors retain authored positions. Clones use the existing fixed180uu offsets and are not silently relocated onto navigation. Per-actor projections expose which sampled locations are navigable; no all-spawn-points guarantee is inferred.
npc_movement.probe_timing_scope: Movement/path/projection probes execute in AfterFrame, outside OnWorldPre/PostActorTick. Their overhead is included in editor end-frame intervals.

active_count_definition: Original NPC class, visible, actor collision enabled, actual AI Blackboard has IsAtHome=false. Actor tick and brain running are reported separately.
world_actor_tick_scope: FPlatformTime span between OnWorldPreActorTick and OnWorldPostActorTick for this PIE world. Includes all actors and intervening world work, not isolated NPC CPU time, a complete game-thread time, or GPU time. Tick starts within the capture window; its completion can cross the final boundary.
frame_interval_scope: Wall-clock intervals between actual game-thread OnEndFrame delegates wholly inside the capture window. Includes editor, PIE, rendering waits, frame caps and instrumentation; not standalone packaged-game FPS or isolated GPU frame time.
memory_scope: Whole editor process physical memory sampled at least 0.25 seconds apart; not per-NPC allocation or an allocation cap. Lifetime OS peak also includes startup and map loading.
